**Strategy: Local Yield Architecture** *A Glocal Pricing & Subscription Model for Emerging-Market Expansion* --- ### Executive Summary Emerging-market growth is no longer about exporting a single USD price tag and accepting high churn. In Africa, South Asia, and Latin America, the friction is not desire for content—it is **mismatch between global billing logic and local cash-flow reality**. Consumers face volatile incomes, communal consumption norms, thin card penetration, and deep aversion to opaque recurring charges. The recommended strategy is the **Local Yield Architecture**: a globally enforced USD contribution-margin floor and normalized reporting standard, overlaid with three **Regional Monetization Models** that localize price points, payment cadence, and household-access rules to match local purchasing power, preferred rails, and social consumption habits. Revenue is consolidated in USD, but the consumer experience is fully indigenous. --- ### I. Strategic Doctrine: Four Global Non-Negotiables Before regional customization, headquarters must establish financial and brand guardrails to prevent a race to the bottom: 1. **The USD Contribution-Margin Floor Is Absolute**: No localized plan—regardless of price point—may be launched unless it delivers positive contribution margin in USD after payment costs, delivery (CDN), and content amortization. A $1.50 plan is permissible only if its unit economics are cleaner than a $12.99 plan with 40% payment failure and high dunning costs. 2. **Prepaid Liquidity Is Not Inferior Revenue**: A daily or weekly top-up is deferred revenue, not a lesser transaction. The platform will treat wallet balances and prepaid bundles as GAAP-compliant deferred income, converting to recognized revenue as days are consumed. Investor optics must evolve: yield matters more than billing modality. 3. **Sharing Is a Market Feature, Not a Fraud**: In these markets, a “household” may span cousins, neighbors, or a joint-family compound. Password crackdowns destroy trust and invite piracy. The platform will monetize communal norms through **social tiers** that explicitly license extended access at a premium-to-individual but discount-to-multiple-accounts price. 4. **PPP-First, FX-Second**: Local prices are anchored to purchasing power parity and local competitive/media spend benchmarks, not to a static exchange-rate conversion. FX risk is centralized: a treasury function hedges major currency exposures and rebalances local prices quarterly to protect USD yield. --- ### II. Regional Monetization Models Deploy the following archetypes, co-designed with local fintechs, mobile-network operators (MNOs), and retail distributors. #### **A. Africa: The “Pulse” Prepaid Model** *Market reality: Card penetration is <5% in many markets; mobile money is the banking system. Data costs often exceed subscription costs. Consumption is communal and cash-flow episodic.* | Dimension | Design | |-----------|--------| | **Price Architecture** | **Daily, weekly, and 30-day passes**, not rigid monthly subscriptions. Entry at ~$0.15/day or ~$2.50/month PPP equivalent.

**Mobile-only SD tier** (1 device, adaptive bitrate to save data). **Home Pass** (5 registered devices / 2 concurrent streams) at ~$4.50 to capture extended-family sharing. | | **Payment Rails** | **Mobile money default**: M-Pesa, MTN MoMo, Airtel Money, OPay. **Carrier billing** via USSD for feature-phone access. **Digital vouchers** sold via MNO agents and street kiosks for pure cash economies.

No credit-card requirement. Auto-renew is opt-in only; default is manual top-up. | | **Billing Psychology** | A **Subscription Wallet**: users buy “streaming days.” The platform draws down one day at a time. This feels like prepaid airtime, eliminating recurring-billing anxiety while generating predictable deferred revenue. | | **Data & Distribution** | **Zero-rating partnerships are non-negotiable.** Negotiate with telcos to zero-rate the app or bundle the subscription with weekly data packs (e.g., “5GB + 7-day streaming”). Revenue-share with telco; platform captures margin without forcing the user to choose between data and content. | | **Sharing Norms** | Do not geo-fence or IP-restrict aggressively. The **Home Pass** tier is priced to be cheaper than two individual subs, making it the rational choice for a compound with three adults. Devices are PIN-registered, not locked by address. | | **Investor Translation** | High volume, very low per-user delivery cost (edge CDN, HEVC mobile encoding), near-zero payment interchange (mobile money fees ~1–2%). Yield per user is modest but CAC is negligible via MNO bundling. | #### **B. South Asia: The “Joint Family Stack”** *Market reality: Extreme price sensitivity, UPI/digital-wallet ubiquity, joint-family households, and a prepaid mobile culture that makes recurring autopay feel alien to mass-market users.* | Dimension | Design | |-----------|--------| | **Price Architecture** | **Mobile-only tier** at ~$1.50–2.00/month (1 screen, phone/tablet). **Standard** at ~$4.00 (2 screens, HD). **Joint Family** tier at ~$7.00 (4 concurrent screens, 5 profiles, UHD/downloads).

Price anchoring: Entry tier must be <0.5% of monthly urban minimum wage. | | **Payment Rails** | **UPI Autopay** (India) and wallet pull (bKash, Easypaisa) as the primary rails. **Prepaid annual coupons** sold via e-commerce and kirana networks for giftability. **EMI financing**: Annual plans offered as 12 no-interest installments auto-deducted via UPI or payroll partners—this locks LTV while preserving monthly cash-flow psychology. | | **Billing Psychology** | Quarterly bundles marketed as “Save More” rather than “Subscribe.” Users prepay for 90 days at a 20% discount. Autopay is framed as a “VIP convenience” for premium tiers only. Dunning is managed via WhatsApp/SMS reminders, not email. | | **Sharing Norms** | Explicitly market the Joint Family tier as: *“One plan for parents, siblings, and cousins—no judgment.”* This captures the normalized password-sharing behavior of the market. Use profile PINs to preserve individual recommendations without hard enforcement. | | **Content Bundling** | Bundle with cricket, regional cinema, or local original commitments. In South Asia, the subscription is validated by local content depth, not just the global library. | | **Investor Translation** | Volume market. Blended ARPU is suppressed by the mobile tier, but Joint Family upsell and annual EMI plans drive 40%+ revenue retention. Payment costs are near-zero on UPI (~0%). | #### **C. Latin America: The “Cuotas & QR” Model** *Market reality: Higher absolute incomes than Africa/South Asia, but high inequality and acute currency volatility. Deep fintech penetration (Pix, Mercado Pago); a cultural expectation of installment payments (*pagar en cuotas*); and multi-generational households.* | Dimension | Design | |-----------|--------| | **Price Architecture** | **Mobile tier** ~$2.99. **Estándar** ~$5.99. **Familia** ~$8.99. Prices are indexed to a basket of local minimum wage and competitor (pay-TV) spend.

In hyperinflation markets (e.g., Argentina), prices are **monthly reviewed** and adjusted in local currency to protect USD yield. | | **Payment Rails** | **Pix QR** (Brazil) and **OXXO/Boleto** (Mexico) for cash-to-digital conversion. **Mercado Pago/PSE** wallet integration. **Credit-card cuotas**: Annual subscriptions payable in 3, 6, or 12 interest-free installments. This is not a discount—it is a mandatory cultural interface for middle-class conversion. | | **Billing Psychology** | Monthly recurring is standard, but users may opt for **manual Pix/OXXO renewal** each month to avoid card dunning. The platform sends QR-code push notifications 48 hours before expiration. Annual plans are heavily marketed during *Día del Padre*, Black Friday, and back-to-school seasons. | | **Sharing Norms** | **Familia** tier allows 4 concurrent streams and geographic mobility (e.g., a child at university retains access). Soft geo-fencing: if account sharing exceeds 4 streams, upsell prompt appears rather than block. | | **Inflation Shield** | Local prices are **floating**. A central pricing algorithm adjusts local-currency rates monthly in volatile economies and quarterly in stable ones (Mexico, Brazil, Chile), maintaining a constant USD-equivalent ARPU. Users accept this if framed as “keeping your local price fair.” | | **Investor Translation** | Highest emerging-market ARPU and LTV. Installment plans reduce churn by locking in 12-month commitments. Pix/OXXO reduces payment failure vs. international card processing. | --- ### III. Unified Tier Architecture Regardless of region, the same product skeleton is priced and packaged locally: | Tier | Core Economics | Africa | South Asia | Latin America | |------|----------------|--------|------------|---------------| | **Lite / Mobile** | 1 screen, SD/HD mobile only, ad-supported optional. Highest volume, lowest yield. | $0.15/day or $2.50/mo | ₹149 (~$1.75)/mo | R$15 / MX$59 (~$2.99)/mo | | **Standard** | 2 screens, HD, all devices. The reference ARPU builder. | $3.50/mo | ₹349 (~$4.00)/mo | R$30 / MX$119 (~$5.99)/mo | | **Social / Familia / Home** | 4–5 screens, UHD, downloads, profile PINs. Monetizes communal norms. | $4.50/mo (Home Pass) | ₹649 (~$7.50)/mo (Joint Family) | R$45 / MX$179 (~$8.99)/mo (Familia) | **Pricing Rule**: Local price must fall between **0.3% and 0.8% of monthly urban minimum wage** for the entry tier, and **1.0%–1.5%** for the family tier. This ensures affordability without destroying perceived value. --- ### IV. The Payment & Billing Operating System To make heterogeneous local rails legible to a centralized USD P&L, the platform operates four unified backend mechanisms: #### 1. The Subscription Wallet (Deferred Revenue Engine) - Users purchase **days of access** or top-up balances in local currency. The wallet draws down daily. - **Accounting**: Upon top-up, revenue is deferred and recognized daily. This unifies daily African passes, Indian quarterly bundles, and Brazilian monthly Pix payments into one revenue recognition logic. - **Investor benefit**: Cash is collected upfront (negative working capital), reducing payment default risk to zero. #### 2. Dynamic Payment Orchestration - **Smart routing**: Each market prioritizes the cheapest successful rail (UPI in India ~0%; Pix in Brazil ~0%; mobile money in Kenya ~1%) over expensive international card networks (~3% + FX spread). - **Localized dunning**: Retry logic respects local payday cycles (e.g., retry mobile money on Fridays; retry UPI after the 1st of the month). - **Manual renewals as a feature**: In markets with low trust, a frictionless “tap to renew” WhatsApp message outperforms hidden auto-renew. #### 3. Carrier & Fintech Bundling (Wholesale Layer) - **Telco-direct billing**: The platform sells wholesale access to MNOs and fintech super-apps. The consumer sees the streaming service as “included with my data plan” or “free with my wallet.” The platform books a guaranteed USD fee per activated user, transferring collection risk to the partner. - **Co-marketing**: Partners absorb CAC; platform captures net-new subs at negative marginal marketing cost. #### 4. Installment & Credit Layer - Partner with local fintechs (e.g., Oxxo Pay, Postpe, Mercado Crédito) to offer 0% interest annual plans. The platform pays a 3–5% financing fee but secures 12-month locked revenue and eliminates monthly churn. --- ### V. Consolidated Unit Economics & Investor Narrative Headquarters reports in USD. To make decentralized pricing defensible, the platform adopts a standardized internal currency and clear margin logic. #### 1. The Normalized Subscriber Unit (NSU) All payment cadences are converted to a 30-day equivalent for reporting: - A Kenyan user on a 7-day pass used 3 weeks/month = 0.75 NSU. - An Indian user on an annual EMI = 1.0 NSU. - A Brazilian user on a 6-month Family plan = 1.0 NSU. **Investor reporting**: “We ended the quarter with 12.4M NSUs in emerging markets, generating a blended $3.85 NSU ARPU and a 22%
